question: Which of the following scientists grouped the elements into triads?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Johann Wolfgang Dobereiner**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Johann Wolfgang Döbereiner, a German chemist,** was one of the first to classify elements based on their similar properties.
 
• In 1829, **he observed that certain groups of three elements had similar chemical properties **and
 
 
• that the atomic mass of the middle element was roughly the average of the other two.
 
 
 
• These **groups of three elements became known as "Döbereiner’s Triads."**
 
• **For example**:
 
 
• Lithium, Sodium, Potassium: In this triad, sodium’s atomic mass is the average of lithium and potassium.
 
• Chlorine, Bromine, Iodine: These elements also formed a triad with similar chemical behavior.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **John Newlands**

 
 
• **Newlands proposed the Law of Octaves**, where he arranged elements in increasing order of atomic mass and noticed that every eighth element had similar properties.
 
• His **work was an important step toward the development of the modern periodic table,** but it was initially criticized for not being applicable to all elements.
 
• His classification system was later recognized as a precursor to Mendeleev’s work.
 
 
 
• **Henry Moseley**
 
 
• Moseley **established the concept of atomic numb**er, which is the number of protons in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• His work showed that elements are better arranged by increasing atomic number rather than atomic mass, leading to a more accurate periodic table.
 
• **His research resolved inconsistencies in Mendeleev’s periodic table.**
 
 
 
• **Dmitri Mendeleev**
 
 
• Mendeleev is **credited with creating the first widely recognized periodic table in 1869.**
 
• He **arranged elements by increasing atomic mass **and left gaps for undiscovered elements, predicting their properties with great accuracy.
 
• Mendeleev’s periodic law laid the groundwork for modern chemistry.
